question: The major focus of my recent travels has been visiting all of the UNESCO World Heritage sites. When I visit a new country, I feel like it helps me appreciate where I am staying for more than just a few popular sites I have seen on social media. I have been paying special attention to what they call "The List in Danger," and I like to prioritize those locations if possible. I have recently visited Cameroon and Chad, and I think that my next destination will be the Democratic Republic of the Congo in June 2025. While I am there, it is my dream to see a Kordofan giraffe. Where could I see them when I visit?

answer:
**Where to see the Kordofan giraffe in the Democratic Republic of the Congo** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Habitat** | **Garamba National Park** (also known as **Garamba NP**), Haut‑Uélé Province, northeast DRC | | **Why it matters** | Garamba is the *only* site in the world where the critically‑endangered **Kordofan giraffe** (_Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum_) has a large, actively monitored wild population (≈ 100 + individuals as of 2024). | | **UNESCO status** | *World Heritage Site* (since 1980). It was on the List of World Heritage in Danger from 1996 to 2002 due to poaching, conflict, and loss of wildlife. The danger status was removed in 2002 because of effective conservation interventions by African Parks and the Gambia Conservation Foundation (GCF). It is **not** on the current Danger list (as of 2024). | | **When to visit** | **June** is part of the short dry season (May–July) in the eastern DRC, when water sources are still plentiful and animals congregate in open savannas. If you plan the trip for June–mid‑July, you’ll have good visibility for giraffes and other wildlife. The park has a *second seasonal flood* (Oct–Feb), which can make access harder. | | **How to get there** | 1. **Fly into Goma** (international hub, ~2 h flight from Kinshasa or Kigali). 2. Take a **4‑hour, 3‑day** bush‑car or charter to Garamba’s gate in Haut‑Uélé (the road is unsealed, so weather matters). 3. Many visitors arrive via the **Goma–Ingende–Garamba** route; you’ll join the official tour convoy. | | **Getting a tour** | - **African Parks** runs the official **Garamba Park Safari** (GAP). Reservations are made through their website or through travel agencies in Kinshasa/Goma.
- **Local charter operators** such as *Eagle Safari*, *Kongola Tours*, or *Dacapo Tours* also provide guided trips, but the park’s manager (African Parks) requires *official tourist permits* for entry. | | **What you’ll see** | - **Kordofan giraffe**: Their distinctive pale patches extending to the lower legs make them recognizable.
- **Other fauna**: Forest elephants, hippopotamuses, Nile crocodiles, black‑backed jackals, Bongo antelopes, and the endemic **Okapi**.
- **Flora**: Dense riverine forests interspersed with open grasslands. | | **Duration** | The standard safari lasts **3–4 days** (including travel to the park), giving ample time for wildlife viewing (dawn & dusk drives). Some tour operators offer a **week‑long** adventure that includes a visit to the **Okapi Wildlife Reserve** nearby. | | **Practical tips** | 1. **Health**: Vaccinations (MMR, hepatitis, typhoid, yellow fever, meningitis). 2. **Malaria**: Take prophylaxis (e.g., Malarone) and bed nets. 3. **Permits**: You will need a *tourist permit* issued by the DRC's Ministry of Tourism, typically handled by the tour operator. 4. **Hazards**: Avoid the Goma region during periods of insurgency (rare, but several border villages have had occasional raids). 5. **Currency**: The Zambian Kwacha (ZMW) is accepted in the park; also have some Euros for the airline and port fees. 6. **Dress**: Light, neutral‑colored clothing; no bright colors (they attract flies). 7. **Photography**: Bring good binoculars (10‑30×) and a telephoto lens (300 mm+) for close‑up giraffe shots. 8. **Sustainability**: Stick to official paths, keep noise low, and carry out any refuse. 9. **Accommodation**: The park offers a basic lodge inside the park (small cabins); outside the park, many lodgings and camps exist near Goma. | | **Contact info** | • **African Parks – Garamba**
Email: garamba@africanparks.org
Phone: +243 509 834 770 (Goma office)
• **Garamba NP Visitor Centre**
Phone/Whatsapp: +243 880 944 944
• **Official website** https://www.africanparks.org/the-parks/garamba | | **Where else to see them?** | The Kordofan giraffe’s historic range also includes parts of northern Cameroon, southern Chad, and the Central African Republic. However, the only *secure*, *publicly accessible* site for a guaranteed view is Garamba. In those other countries, giraffes are typically fewer, threatened, and access is restricted or non‑existent for tourism. | | **Quick FAQ** | **Q:** Are the giraffes easy to spot?
A: Along the **riverine corridors** and in the scattered **grass‑lawn patches** they are relatively easy to spot, especially during the dry season.
**Q:** Do I need a guide?
A: Yes – a licensed guide is mandatory for entry and a key part of the conservation effort.
**Q:** Can I camp in the park?
A: Only in designated sites (within the park, under the park's management). | | **Optional add‑ons** | • **Okapi Visit** – a short trip to Okapi Wildlife Reserve (2–3 days).
• **Birdwatching** – Garamba hosts > 300 bird species; bring a good binocular sheet.
• **Photography workshop** – some tour operators offer a 6‑hour workshop on wildlife photography with a local photographer. | **Bottom line for your June 2025 trip:** If you’re set on seeing Kordofan giraffes, the only reliable, UNESCO‑backed location is *Garamba National Park*. Book your **African Parks safari** (or a certified tour operator), arrive via Goma, and enjoy a stunning, conserved glimpse of one of the world’s most endangered giraffe subspecies. Happy travels—and may your photographs capture those striking pale‑patch giraffes!

# Kordofan Giraffe Conservation in DRC
Garamba National Park in DRC is the last haven for the Kordofan giraffe in the country. Despite threats from poaching and rebel activities, GCF, African Parks, and the DRC government have successfully achieved a steady increase in giraffe numbers.

In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Garamba National Park is home to the last remaining population of Kordofan giraffe (_Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum_), a subspecies of the northern giraffe (_Giraffa camelopardalis_). Established in 1938 as one of Africa’s first national parks, Garamba stood out for its uniqueness. However, its reputation has been marred by the activities of rebel insurgents (Lord’s Resistance Army) resulting in the loss of the last northern white rhino.
Over the past few decades, poaching has decimated the park’s wildlife, as rebel groups often resort to selling wildlife products to fund their illegal activities. Recognizing the dire situation, the Giraffe Conservation Foundation has collaborated with African Parks and DRC’s wildlife authority, ICCN, since 2016 to save the last natural giraffe population in the country.
Our collaborative efforts have focused on gaining a deeper understanding of population dynamics, habitat use, and immediate threats. The team of African Parks, with the support of the Giraffe Conservation Foundation, implements conservation monitoring and management activities through regular aerial and vehicle-based surveys to monitor all individually-identified giraffe.
The targeted giraffe conservation efforts have resulted in Kordofan giraffe numbers in the park and surrounding areas gradually increasing to over 100 giraffe. This positive trend underscores the importance of continued support for this crucial giraffe conservation initiative, which is slowly transforming into a remarkable success story.

**Where to see the Kordofan giraffe in the Democratic Republic of the Congo** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Habitat** | **Garamba National Park** (also known as **Garamba NP**), Haut‑Uélé Province, northeast DRC | | **Why it matters** | Garamba is the *only* site in the world where the critically‑endangered **Kordofan giraffe** (_Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum_) has a large, actively monitored wild population (≈ 100 + individuals as of 2024). | | **UNESCO status** | *World Heritage Site* (since 1980). It was on the List of World Heritage in Danger from 1996 to 2002 due to poaching, conflict, and loss of wildlife. The danger status was removed in 2002 because of effective conservation interventions by African Parks and the Gambia Conservation Foundation (GCF). It is **not** on the current Danger list (as of 2024). | | **When to visit** | **June** is part of the short dry season (May–July) in the eastern DRC, when water sources are still plentiful and animals congregate in open savannas. If you plan the trip for June–mid‑July, you’ll have good visibility for giraffes and other wildlife. The park has a *second seasonal flood* (Oct–Feb), which can make access harder. | | **How to get there** | 1. **Fly into Goma** (international hub, ~2 h flight from Kinshasa or Kigali). 2. Take a **4‑hour, 3‑day** bush‑car or charter to Garamba’s gate in Haut‑Uélé (the road is unsealed, so weather matters). 3. Many visitors arrive via the **Goma–Ingende–Garamba** route; you’ll join the official tour convoy. | | **Getting a tour** | - **African Parks** runs the official **Garamba Park Safari** (GAP). Reservations are made through their website or through travel agencies in Kinshasa/Goma.
- **Local charter operators** such as *Eagle Safari*, *Kongola Tours*, or *Dacapo Tours* also provide guided trips, but the park’s manager (African Parks) requires *official tourist permits* for entry. | | **What you’ll see** | - **Kordofan giraffe**: Their distinctive pale patches extending to the lower legs make them recognizable.
- **Other fauna**: Forest elephants, hippopotamuses, Nile crocodiles, black‑backed jackals, Bongo antelopes, and the endemic **Okapi**.
- **Flora**: Dense riverine forests interspersed with open grasslands. | | **Duration** | The standard safari lasts **3–4 days** (including travel to the park), giving ample time for wildlife viewing (dawn & dusk drives). Some tour operators offer a **week‑long** adventure that includes a visit to the **Okapi Wildlife Reserve** nearby. | | **Practical tips** | 1. **Health**: Vaccinations (MMR, hepatitis, typhoid, yellow fever, meningitis). 2. **Malaria**: Take prophylaxis (e.g., Malarone) and bed nets. 3. **Permits**: You will need a *tourist permit* issued by the DRC's Ministry of Tourism, typically handled by the tour operator. 4. **Hazards**: Avoid the Goma region during periods of insurgency (rare, but several border villages have had occasional raids). 5. **Currency**: The Zambian Kwacha (ZMW) is accepted in the park; also have some Euros for the airline and port fees. 6. **Dress**: Light, neutral‑colored clothing; no bright colors (they attract flies). 7. **Photography**: Bring good binoculars (10‑30×) and a telephoto lens (300 mm+) for close‑up giraffe shots. 8. **Sustainability**: Stick to official paths, keep noise low, and carry out any refuse. 9. **Accommodation**: The park offers a basic lodge inside the park (small cabins); outside the park, many lodgings and camps exist near Goma. | | **Contact info** | • **African Parks – Garamba**
Email: garamba@africanparks.org
Phone: +243 509 834 770 (Goma office)
• **Garamba NP Visitor Centre**
Phone/Whatsapp: +243 880 944 944
• **Official website** https://www.africanparks.org/the-parks/garamba | | **Where else to see them?** | The Kordofan giraffe’s historic range also includes parts of northern Cameroon, southern Chad, and the Central African Republic. However, the only *secure*, *publicly accessible* site for a guaranteed view is Garamba. In those other countries, giraffes are typically fewer, threatened, and access is restricted or non‑existent for tourism. | | **Quick FAQ** | **Q:** Are the giraffes easy to spot?
A: Along the **riverine corridors** and in the scattered **grass‑lawn patches** they are relatively easy to spot, especially during the dry season.
**Q:** Do I need a guide?
A: Yes – a licensed guide is mandatory for entry and a key part of the conservation effort.
**Q:** Can I camp in the park?
A: Only in designated sites (within the park, under the park's management). | | **Optional add‑ons** | • **Okapi Visit** – a short trip to Okapi Wildlife Reserve (2–3 days).
• **Birdwatching** – Garamba hosts > 300 bird species; bring a good binocular sheet.
• **Photography workshop** – some tour operators offer a 6‑hour workshop on wildlife photography with a local photographer. | **Bottom line for your June 2025 trip:** If you’re set on seeing Kordofan giraffes, the only reliable, UNESCO‑backed location is *Garamba National Park*. Book your **African Parks safari** (or a certified tour operator), arrive via Goma, and enjoy a stunning, conserved glimpse of one of the world’s most endangered giraffe subspecies. Happy travels—and may your photographs capture those striking pale‑patch giraffes!
